docs.title: Ethical Hacking
docs.text: Hands-on · CEH-aligned

docs.title: Attack it. Defend it. Report it.
docs.text:
A hands-on, CEH-aligned introduction to ethical hacking — you'll scan, test, exploit, and secure systems in a safe virtual lab, then learn to write up what you found like a professional.

4.5 units 48 lecture + 18 lab hrs CEH exam-aligned Hands-on ACI Skill Labs Open-access readings — $0

docs.title: The course in five phases
docs.text: This course follows the real attacker's kill chain — the same arc a professional penetration tester walks through on an engagement — while covering the full set of CEH topic areas.

docs.title: Foundation
docs.text: Week 1. Ethics, law, authorization, and the five-phase methodology. The rules before the tools.

docs.title: Recon & Scanning
docs.text: Weeks 2–3. Footprinting, OSINT, network scanning with Nmap, and enumeration.

docs.title: Network & Crypto
docs.text: Weeks 4–5. Sniffing, IDS/firewall/honeypot evasion, and cryptography (PKI, certificates, attacks).

docs.title: System & Malware
docs.text: Weeks 6–7. Windows/Linux exploitation, privilege escalation, trojans, malware, DoS, and session hijacking.

docs.title: Human & Web
docs.text: Weeks 8–10. Social engineering, web-server and web-app attacks, and a SQL-injection deep dive.

docs.title: Wireless & Pentest
docs.text: Weeks 11–12. Wi-Fi (WEP/WPA) attacks, then a full penetration-test methodology and a capstone report.

docs.title: What you'll be able to do
docs.text:
By the end of the quarter you will be able to demonstrate the ability to attack and defend a network — the course's core learning outcome — and you'll be prepared for the Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH) exam. Concretely, you'll be able to:

  • Conduct reconnaissance and map a target's attack surface.
  • Scan and enumerate hosts, services, and vulnerabilities.
  • Exploit systems and web applications in a controlled lab.
  • Recognize and reason about malware, DoS, and social-engineering attacks.
  • Apply cryptographic concepts and evade basic network defenses.
  • Plan a penetration test and write a professional findings report.

docs.title: How the course is delivered
docs.text:
Three moving parts

Lecture (concepts, in class) · Labs (hands-on, ACI Skill Labs) · Reading (free, open-access — linked on every week page). There is no textbook to buy.

  • Hands-on labs run on ACI Skill Labs. Every lab includes a guided walkthrough, a live virtual machine, and auto-graded checkpoints.
  • Readings are all free and open-access — NIST guides, OWASP, the official Nmap book, Crypto 101, Metasploit Unleashed, and more. See the Free Resource Library.
  • Ethics and law run through the whole course, anchored by Alana Maurushat's open-access Ethical Hacking.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Read the Syllabus for policies, grading, and the week-1 setup steps.
  • New to the tools? Skim Kali Linux Revealed before Week 3.
  • Jump to Week 1.

Authorization first

Everything in this course is practiced only inside the provided lab environment or on systems you have explicit written permission to test. Unauthorized access to computer systems is a crime. You'll sign an acceptable-use agreement in Week 1.

docs.title: Course description
docs.text:
Students will scan, test, hack, and secure systems; implement perimeter defenses; and scan and attack virtual networks. Coverage includes intrusion detection, social engineering, footprinting, DDoS attacks, buffer overflows, SQL injection, privilege escalation, trojans, backdoors, and wireless hacking, with emphasis on legal and ethical guidelines. The course prepares students for the Certified Ethical Hacker (C|EH) exam.

Format Lecture + hands-on lab Course outcome Demonstrate the ability to attack and defend a network. Advisories Prior coursework in networking and operating systems recommended Textbook None to buy — all readings are free/open-access Lab platform ACI Skill Labs

docs.title: Course objectives
docs.text:
1. Explore ethical hacking fundamentals
  2. Explore cryptographic concepts
  3. Investigate reconnaissance and information gathering
  4. Explore scanning and enumeration
  5. Explore network hacking via sniffers and evasion
  6. Investigate system attacks
  7. Explore low-tech hacking techniques
  8. Investigate web-based hacking
  9. Explore wireless network hacking
  10. Investigate trojans and related attacks
  11. Perform penetration testing

docs.title: Grading
docs.text: Component Weight Notes Hands-on labs (auto-graded) 35% ACI Skill Labs — Performance Reports Midterm exam 15% Units 1–6, CEH-style Final exam 15% Cumulative, CEH-style Capstone penetration-test report 20% Methodology + professional deliverable Ethics paper + participation 15% Maurushat-based paper, discussions

docs.title: Week-1 setup checklist
docs.text:
Do these in the first week

  1. Get your institutional email set up (needed for any external sign-ups).
  2. Log in to the ACI Skill Labs portal and confirm you can launch a lab VM (the Start button) — run the Week-2 recon lab's intro to test it.
  3. Bookmark the Free Resource Library.
  4. Read and sign the Acceptable-Use / Authorization Agreement.
  5. Skim Maurushat, Ethical Hacking, Introduction (open-access — see Week 1).

docs.title: Academic integrity & ethics
docs.text: The skills in this course are powerful and, misused, illegal. You will practice them only in the provided lab environment or against systems you have explicit written authorization to test. Any attack against systems, networks, or accounts without authorization is a violation of course policy and of state and federal law, and may result in course failure and possible referral. When in doubt, ask before you act.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text: Students who need accommodations should contact their institution's disability support office and let the instructor know early in the term so arrangements can be made for lecture, labs, and exams.

docs.title: Coverage notes
docs.text:
Fully covered by labs

Reconnaissance, scanning/enumeration, sniffing, system exploitation, malware/DoS, web attacks (strong), SQL injection, cryptography, and Wi-Fi — all have launchable, graded ACI Skill Labs.

Covered by lecture + assignment (not a lab)

  • Ethics & law (Unit 1) — lecture + Maurushat reading + discussion/paper.
  • Pentest methodology & deliverables (Unit 11) — lecture + capstone report.
  • Bluetooth, honeypots/IDS specifics, physical security — lecture sub-topics.

Optional enrichment (in CEH, beyond this course's core units)

IoT/OT and Cloud Computing — add if time allows; ACI has "with AI" concept labs for both. (Covered by CEH but outside this course's core unit list.)

docs.title: Tools Reference
docs.text:
The core tools students will meet, and where in the course they appear. All are available inside the ACI Skill Labs environment (typically Kali Linux) — no local install required.

Tool Used for First appears Nmap Host discovery, port/service scanning, OS fingerprinting, NSE scripts Week 3 Wireshark / tcpdump Packet capture & traffic analysis Weeks 3–4 WHOIS / dig / nslookup Domain & DNS reconnaissance Week 2 Metasploit Framework Exploitation, payloads, Meterpreter post-exploitation Week 6 Password crackers (John, Hashcat, Ophcrack) Offline credential cracking Week 6 Social-Engineer Toolkit (SET) Phishing & credential-harvesting scenarios Week 8 Burp Suite / browser dev tools Web-app testing & interception Weeks 9–10 sqlmap Automated SQL-injection (conceptual + lab) Week 10 Aircrack-ng suite Wireless capture & WEP/WPA cracking Week 11 Nessus / OpenVAS Vulnerability scanning Weeks 3 / 6 (within labs)

Verify the named tools

The course outline specifically lists Metasploit, packet sniffing, WHOIS, port scanning, keylogging, Ophcrack password cracking, DoS, and Nessus. Most appear inside broader ACI labs (e.g., cracking inside System Hacking, Nessus inside Vulnerability Analysis). Open those labs to confirm; demo any missing tool live on a Kali VM.

docs.title: Getting comfortable with Kali
docs.text: Students don't need to install anything, but if you want to explore the toolset behind the labs, Kali Linux Revealed is the free official guide: kali.org/download-kali-linux-revealed-book.

docs.title: Week 1 · Ethics, Law & Methodology
docs.text: Foundation · Unit 1 · CEH Domain 1 (Information Security & Ethical Hacking)

docs.title: The rules before the tools
docs.text: Lecture Setup week Ethics reading

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this week you will be able to:

  • Define ethical hacking and distinguish it from cracking, hacktivism, and cybercrime.
  • Explain the legal boundaries (authorization, scope, rules of engagement) that separate a penetration test from a crime.
  • Describe the five phases of ethical hacking: reconnaissance, scanning, gaining access, maintaining access, and covering tracks.
  • Set up your lab access and understand how the course runs.

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
(Lecture outline — expand in class.)

  • What is ethical hacking? White/grey/black hats; the CEH mindset; think offense to build defense.
  • Types of assessments: vulnerability assessment vs. penetration test vs. red team.
  • Legal & professional frame: authorization letters, scope, rules of engagement, non-disclosure, the CFAA and California Penal Code §502.
  • The five-phase methodology — the backbone of the whole course.
  • Where hacktivism blurs the line — discussion anchored in the Maurushat reading.

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text:
• Alana Maurushat, Ethical Hacking (University of Ottawa Press, 2019) — Introduction + Ch. 1. Open access. Publisher page · Full PDF (OAPEN)
  • NIST SP 800-115, Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment — §1–2 (overview & methodology). Free PDF

docs.title: Lab
docs.text:
No attack lab this week. Instead:

  • Launch ACI Skill Labs → Introduction to AI in Ethical Hacking (concept lab) to confirm your access works end to end.
  • Verify the Start button spins up a VM and that Performance Reports records your completion.

docs.title: Assignment
docs.text:
• Discussion post (graded): Where is the line between ethical hacking and hacktivism? Cite one example from Maurushat. (200–300 words.)
  • Sign the Acceptable-Use / Authorization Agreement in Canvas.
  • Complete the Week-1 setup checklist on the Syllabus.

docs.title: Week 2 · Reconnaissance & Footprinting
docs.text: Recon & Scanning · Unit 3 · CEH Domain 2 (Reconnaissance Techniques)

docs.title: Know the target before you touch it
docs.text: Lecture + Lab 2 labs OSINT

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Distinguish passive from active reconnaissance.
  • Use OSINT sources, WHOIS, DNS, and search-engine techniques to profile a target.
  • Assemble a footprint: domains, hosts, emails, technologies, and exposure.

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
• Passive vs. active recon; why passive comes first (stealth, legality).
  • WHOIS & DNS — registrars, name servers, zone data, subdomain discovery.
  • OSINT — search operators / Google dorking, certificate transparency, job posts, metadata.
  • Footprinting outputs — how recon feeds scanning and social engineering later.

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text:
• NIST SP 800-115 §4 (Review & Target Identification techniques). Free PDF
  • OSINT Framework — browse the categories to see the breadth of open sources. osintframework.com
  • MITRE ATT&CK — Reconnaissance tactic (TA0043). attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0043

docs.title: Labs (ACI Skill Labs)
docs.text:
1. Footprinting and Reconnaissance Techniques with AI (concept primer)
  2. Performing Reconnaissance from the WAN (graded — banner grabbing, external recon, credential capture)

docs.title: Assignment
docs.text:
• Complete both labs (auto-graded).
  • Mini-report: Footprint a provided practice domain and submit a one-page recon summary (assets found, methods used, what a defender should hide).

docs.title: Week 3 · Scanning & Enumeration
docs.text: Recon & Scanning · Unit 4 · CEH Domain 2 (Scanning & Enumeration)

docs.title: Find the doors, then knock on them
docs.text: Lecture + Lab 2 labs Nmap Quiz

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Perform host discovery and port/service scanning with Nmap.
  • Interpret scan results: open/closed/filtered, service and OS fingerprints.
  • Enumerate services (SMB, SNMP, SMTP, etc.) to extract users, shares, and configuration.

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
• Scanning types — TCP connect, SYN, UDP; timing and stealth.
  • Nmap in depth — host discovery, -sV, -O, NSE scripts.
  • Enumeration — turning "a port is open" into "here's the version, users, and shares."
  • Defender's view — what scanning looks like in logs and to an IDS (previews Week 4).

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text:
• Nmap Network Scanning (the official Nmap book, Gordon "Fyodor" Lyon) — Host Discovery & Port Scanning chapters. nmap.org/book
  • NIST SP 800-115 §4.2 (Network scanning), §4.3 (Vulnerability scanning). Free PDF

docs.title: Labs (ACI Skill Labs)
docs.text:
1. Scanning the Network on the LAN (graded)
  2. Enumerating Hosts Using Wireshark, Windows, and Linux Commands (graded)

docs.title: Assignment
docs.text:
• Complete both labs.
  • Quiz (Units 3–4): recon, scanning, and enumeration.

docs.title: Week 4 · Network Hacking & Sniffing
docs.text: Network & Crypto · Unit 5 · CEH Domain 3 (System Hacking Phases & Network)

docs.title: Listen on the wire, then slip past the guards
docs.text: Lecture + Lab 2 labs Wireshark

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Capture and analyze network traffic with a sniffer.
  • Explain how ARP spoofing / MITM exposes cleartext data.
  • Describe IDS, firewalls, and honeypots — and common evasion techniques.

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
• Sniffing — promiscuous mode, span ports, active vs. passive sniffing, ARP poisoning.
  • Reading traffic — following streams, extracting credentials from cleartext protocols.
  • Network defenses — IDS/IPS signatures, firewall rule types, honeypots.
  • Evasion — tunneling, encryption, fragmentation; why exfil over an encrypted channel is hard to catch.

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text:
• Wireshark User's Guide — capturing & analyzing traffic. wireshark.org/docs
  • MITRE ATT&CK — Network Sniffing (T1040) and Defense Evasion (TA0005). T1040 · TA0005

docs.title: Labs (ACI Skill Labs)
docs.text:
1. Capturing and Analyzing Network Traffic Using a Sniffer (graded)
  2. Attacking the Firewall and Stealing Data Over an Encrypted Channel (graded — evasion/exfiltration)

docs.title: Assignment
docs.text:
• Complete both labs.
  • Short answer: From a provided capture, identify the protocol, extract the leaked data, and recommend one defense.

docs.title: Week 5 · Cryptography
docs.text: Network & Crypto · Unit 2 · CEH Domain 7 (Cryptography)

docs.title: The math that protects — and how it fails
docs.text: Lecture + Lab 2 labs PKI

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Distinguish symmetric vs. asymmetric encryption and explain where each is used.
  • Explain PKI: public/private keys, digital certificates, and certificate authorities.
  • Describe hashing, digital signatures, and common cryptographic attacks.

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
• Symmetric (AES) vs. asymmetric (RSA, ECC); key exchange.
  • PKI — CAs, chains of trust, X.509 certificates, TLS handshake at a high level.
  • Hashing & integrity — MD5/SHA, salting, why hashes ≠ encryption.
  • Attacks — brute force, birthday, downgrade, padding-oracle (conceptual), weak-key.

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text: • Crypto 101 (Laurens Van Houtven) — free book. Read Ch. 1–7 (block ciphers, stream ciphers, key exchange, public-key, hashes). crypto101.io

docs.title: Labs (ACI Skill Labs)
docs.text:
1. Cryptography Techniques with AI (concept primer)
  2. Using Public Key Encryption to Secure Messages (graded)

docs.title: Assignment
docs.text:
• Complete both labs.
  • Exercise: Generate a keypair, sign and verify a message, and explain in a paragraph what a certificate adds on top of a raw public key.

docs.title: Week 6 · System Attacks · Midterm
docs.text: System & Malware · Unit 6 · CEH Domain 3 (System Hacking)

docs.title: Gaining access — and keeping it
docs.text: Lecture + Lab 2 labs Metasploit Midterm

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Exploit vulnerable Windows and Linux systems in the lab.
  • Explain privilege escalation and post-exploitation (maintaining access, covering tracks).
  • Use a framework (Metasploit) to deliver and manage an exploit.

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
• Exploitation basics — matching a vulnerability to an exploit; payloads and shells.
  • Metasploit — modules, msfconsole, Meterpreter.
  • Privilege escalation — Windows vs. Linux paths; credential dumping.
  • Post-exploitation — persistence, pivoting, anti-forensics (and why defenders watch for it).

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text:
• Metasploit Unleashed (OffSec) — free course/book: fundamentals, exploitation, Meterpreter. offsec.com/metasploit-unleashed
  • Kali Linux Revealed — relevant tooling chapters. kali.org book

docs.title: Labs (ACI Skill Labs)
docs.text:
1. Remote and Local Exploitation (graded)
  2. Using Browser Exploitation to Take Over a Host's Computer (graded)

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
• Complete both labs.
  • Midterm exam — Units 1–6 (CEH-style).

docs.title: Week 7 · Trojans, Malware & DoS
docs.text: System & Malware · Unit 10 · CEH Domain 3 (Malware, DoS, Session Hijacking)

docs.title: Payloads, floods, and stolen sessions
docs.text: Lecture + Lab 2 labs RAT / DoS

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Classify malware: viruses, worms, trojans, RATs, ransomware.
  • Explain how a Remote Access Trojan is built, delivered, and detected.
  • Describe denial-of-service and session-hijacking attacks and their defenses.

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
• Malware taxonomy — propagation vs. payload; droppers, backdoors, RATs.
  • RAT lifecycle — build, deliver, C2, persistence; AV evasion at a high level.
  • DoS/DDoS — volumetric, protocol, application-layer; amplification.
  • Session hijacking — token theft, fixation, MITM; why HTTPS + secure cookies matter.

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text:
• MITRE ATT&CK — Command and Control (TA0011), Impact/Endpoint DoS (T1499). TA0011 · T1499
  • CISA — Understanding Denial-of-Service Attacks. cisa.gov/news-events/news/understanding-denial-service-attacks

docs.title: Labs (ACI Skill Labs)
docs.text:
1. Crafting and Deploying Malware Using a Remote Access Trojan (RAT) (graded)
  2. Performing a Denial of Service Attack from the WAN (graded)

docs.title: Assignment
docs.text:
• Complete both labs.
  • Short answer: For the RAT you deployed, list three detection or prevention controls a defender could use at different layers.

docs.title: Week 8 · Social Engineering
docs.text: Human & Web · Unit 7 · CEH Domain 3 (Social Engineering)

docs.title: The easiest exploit is a person
docs.text: Lecture + Lab 1 lab SET Ethics paper

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Explain the psychology behind social-engineering attacks.
  • Use the Social-Engineer Toolkit (SET) to build a phishing scenario in the lab.
  • Recommend awareness and technical controls; reason about the ethics of pretexting.

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
• Principles of influence — authority, urgency, reciprocity, trust.
  • Vectors — phishing, spear-phishing, vishing, pretexting, tailgating, physical.
  • SET — credential-harvesting and payload attacks (lab).
  • Defense — awareness training, MFA, reporting culture, technical filtering.
  • Ethics — consent and harm in social-engineering tests (Maurushat tie-in).

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text:
• MITRE ATT&CK — Phishing (T1566) and the Initial Access tactic. T1566
  • CISA — Avoiding Social Engineering and Phishing Attacks. cisa.gov/news-events/news/avoiding-social-engineering-and-phishing-attacks
  • Maurushat, Ethical Hacking — chapter on the ethics of deception/consent.

docs.title: Lab (ACI Skill Labs)
docs.text: • Social Engineering Attacks Using SET (graded)

docs.title: Assignment
docs.text:
• Complete the lab.
  • Ethics paper (graded, ~1000 words): When is a social-engineering test ethical? Argue a position using Maurushat and one real-world case.

docs.title: Week 9 · Web Attacks I
docs.text: Human & Web · Unit 8 · CEH Domain 3 (Web Server & Web App Hacking)

docs.title: The web is the biggest attack surface
docs.text: Lecture + Lab 2 labs OWASP

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Describe the web-server and web-application attack surface.
  • Walk through the OWASP Top 10 and map each to a real risk.
  • Exploit a vulnerable web application in the lab (auth, access-control, injection points).

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
• Web-server attacks — misconfig, default creds, outdated components, directory traversal.
  • Web-app attacks — broken access control, injection, XSS, CSRF, insecure design.
  • The OWASP Top 10 as a shared vocabulary.
  • Methodology — map → discover → exploit → document (previews the WSTG in Week 10).

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text:
• OWASP Top 10 — read every category. owasp.org/www-project-top-ten
  • OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG) — Introduction & testing framework. owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide

docs.title: Labs (ACI Skill Labs)
docs.text:
1. Attacking Webservers from the WAN (graded)
  2. Exploiting a Vulnerable Web Application (graded)

docs.title: Assignment
docs.text:
• Complete both labs.
  • Map-it exercise: For the vulnerable app, tie two findings to specific OWASP Top 10 categories and propose fixes.

docs.title: Week 10 · Web Attacks II — SQL Injection
docs.text: Human & Web · Unit 8 · CEH Domain 3 (SQL Injection)

docs.title: One quote mark to own the database
docs.text: Lecture + Lab 2 labs SQLi Quiz

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Explain how SQL injection works and why it remains so damaging.
  • Perform in-band, blind, and error-based SQLi in the lab.
  • Recommend parameterized queries, input validation, and least-privilege as defenses.
  • (Lecture) Relate XSS and CSRF as sibling web-injection attacks.

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
• SQLi mechanics — untrusted input concatenated into a query; classic ' OR 1=1.
  • Variants — union-based, error-based, boolean/time-based blind.
  • Automation — how tools like sqlmap scale it (conceptual/lab).
  • Defense — prepared statements/parameterization, ORM, input validation, DB permissions, WAF.
  • XSS & CSRF (lecture) — stored/reflected XSS, CSRF tokens.

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text:
• OWASP — SQL Injection and the WSTG injection-testing section. SQL Injection · WSTG
  • OWASP Cheat Sheet — SQL Injection Prevention. cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html

docs.title: Labs (ACI Skill Labs)
docs.text:
1. Performing SQL Injection to Manipulate Tables in a Database (graded)
  2. SQL Injection Methodologies with AI (concept primer)

docs.title: Assignment
docs.text:
• Complete both labs.
  • Quiz (Unit 8): web-server, web-app, and SQL-injection attacks + defenses.

docs.title: Week 11 · Wireless Hacking
docs.text: Wireless & Pentest · Unit 9 · CEH Domain 4 (Wireless)

docs.title: Attacks that travel through the air
docs.text: Lecture + Lab 1 lab WEP/WPA

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Explain Wi-Fi security: WEP, WPA/WPA2/WPA3, and their weaknesses.
  • Capture wireless traffic and crack WEP/WPA keys in the lab.
  • Describe Bluetooth attack surface at a conceptual level (lecture).

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
• Wireless architecture — SSIDs, APs, association, the 4-way handshake.
  • WEP — why it's broken (IV reuse); WPA/WPA2 — handshake capture + dictionary attack; WPA3 improvements.
  • Aircrack-ng workflow — monitor mode, capture, crack.
  • Bluetooth (lecture) — bluejacking/bluesnarfing, BLE exposure.
  • Defense — WPA3, strong passphrases, 802.1X, rogue-AP detection.

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text:
• Aircrack-ng documentation & tutorials — WEP/WPA cracking workflow. aircrack-ng.org/documentation.html
  • MITRE ATT&CK — (network) Adversary-in-the-Middle & wireless-relevant techniques. attack.mitre.org

docs.title: Lab (ACI Skill Labs)
docs.text: • Breaking WEP and WPA and Decrypting the Traffic (graded)

docs.title: Assignment
docs.text:
• Complete the lab.
  • Short answer: Explain why capturing the WPA2 handshake doesn't instantly reveal the key, and what makes a passphrase crackable.

docs.title: Week 12 · Penetration Testing & Capstone
docs.text: Wireless & Pentest · Unit 11 · CEH Domain 1 (Methodology & Reporting)

docs.title: Put it all together — and write it up
docs.text: Lecture + Capstone Final exam Report

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Describe a full penetration-testing methodology end to end.
  • Scope an engagement: rules of engagement, authorization, boundaries.
  • Analyze findings and produce a professional penetration-test report with prioritized remediation.

docs.title: Concept notes
docs.text:
• Methodology — pre-engagement → recon → scanning → exploitation → post-exploitation → reporting.
  • Frameworks — NIST SP 800-115, PTES, OSSTMM; how they compare.
  • Deliverables — executive summary, findings with severity (CVSS), evidence, remediation.
  • Professionalism — retest, disclosure, client communication.

docs.title: Reading (free)
docs.text:
• NIST SP 800-115 — full document, focus on §5–8 (analysis, reporting, remediation). Free PDF
  • Penetration Testing Execution Standard (PTES) — Reporting section. pentest-standard.org

docs.title: Capstone
docs.text: Choose a set of the quarter's lab targets and run a mini end-to-end engagement (recon → exploit → document).

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
• Capstone penetration-test report (graded, 20%) — professional deliverable: scope, methodology, findings with severity, evidence, and remediation.
  • Final exam — cumulative, CEH-style.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Sit the CEH exam (you've now covered the domains).
  • Explore Cloud and IoT/OT hacking (CEH modules beyond this course's outline) as optional enrichment — see the Free Resource Library.
